articles.title: Thailand Drafts 5 Million Baht Daily Cap on Stablecoin Transfers
articles.excerpt: Transfers would only be allowed between a customer's own verified wallets. Moves between two Thai licensed platforms escape the cap. Comments close Nov. 26.
articles.body_md:
Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission wants to limit how many stablecoins a person can move in and out of a licensed crypto platform: 5 million baht (about $148,000) each way, per day, per platform. The draft rules were published Thursday, and [comments are due Nov. 26](https://www.sec.or.th/TH/Pages/News_Detail.aspx?SECID=13561).

The SEC says the goal is to stop money laundering and to stop people from using stablecoins to get around Thailand's rules on sending money abroad. It first floated the plan in a [September consultation](https://www.sec.or.th/EN/Pages/News_Detail.aspx?SECID=13335).

**Your wallet, and only your wallet**

A stablecoin is a crypto token pegged to a currency such as the U.S. dollar, and it can cross borders in minutes without a bank wire. That is the gap the regulator is closing. Under the draft, a customer could deposit stablecoins only from a wallet verified as their own, and withdraw only to one verified the same way. Sending to or receiving from someone else's wallet through a licensed platform would be banned.

Both ends would also have to meet the Travel Rule, the global standard that makes crypto firms collect and pass on sender and recipient details. Platforms would have to screen out mule accounts and run blockchain-tracing tools against watchlisted wallets. Transfer sizes would also have to fit the customer's income and finances, cap or no cap.

**Four groups skip the limit**

The 5 million baht ceiling would not apply to licensed operators moving coins in their own name, businesses the Bank of Thailand has approved case by case to use stablecoins, market makers in stablecoin/baht pairs, and subscriptions or refunds for SEC-approved token offerings. Moves between a customer's own accounts at two Thai licensed platforms aren't capped either, as long as both apply the Travel Rule, the SEC said.

The rules cover licensed platforms only. Purely peer-to-peer transfers on a blockchain fall outside them, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-13-thailand-seeks-daily-stablecoin-cap-439676).

The SEC has not set an effective date.

*In our opinion: the cap gets the headline, but the own-wallet rule is the bigger change. The limit only bites above about $148,000 a day, while the own-wallet rule covers every transfer, so splitting a dinner bill in USDT through a Thai exchange would be off the menu. Nov. 26 is the date to circle, and the final notice will show whether the list of exemptions grows.*

articles.title: DOJ and CFTC Sue Arkansas to Stop Its Case Against Kalshi
articles.excerpt: The federal suit asks a judge to bar Arkansas from investigating any CFTC-regulated exchange and its partners under state gambling law, not just Kalshi.
articles.body_md:
The Justice Department and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Arkansas on Thursday, Nov. 12, asking a federal judge to stop the state's Nov. 4 lawsuit against prediction market Kalshi. The [34-page complaint](https://askspinner.com/news/cftc-doj-sue-arkansas-griffin-kalshi) was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas (No. 4:26-cv-01255).

The case goes beyond one company. The government asks for an injunction barring Arkansas and Attorney General Tim Griffin from investigating CFTC-regulated exchanges "and their affiliates and partners" under state law, [according to the complaint](https://eventmarkets.ai/cftc-and-the-federal-government-sue-arkansas-to-stop-its-kalshi-lawsuit/). Kalshi is not a party.

**Swaps or bets**

A prediction market lets people buy contracts that pay out if an event happens, such as a team winning or a bill passing. The fight is over what those contracts are. The federal agencies argue they are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act, and that the law gives the CFTC "exclusive jurisdiction" over swaps traded on exchanges it designates. Kalshi has held that designation since 2020. If that holds, federal law preempts, or overrides, state gambling rules for those trades.

Arkansas sees it the other way. Griffin's suit, filed in Independence County Circuit Court, alleges Kalshi offers illegal gambling without a state license and violates the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. It seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and an injunction.

"Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," Griffin said in his [Nov. 4 statement](https://arkansasag.gov/news-release/attorney-general-griffin-sues-prediction-market-kalshi-for-providing-illegal-gambling-platform-in-arkansas/), adding that wagering on whether the Razorbacks win "is gambling." His statement also acknowledged that Kalshi disputes the gambling label.

**No reply yet from Little Rock**

We found no public response from Griffin's office to the federal suit by 6 a.m. ET Friday. [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-13-doj-cftc-sue-arkansas-to-block-state-enforcement-action-against-kalshi-439669) it had asked Kalshi and Griffin's office for comment. None of the claims in either lawsuit has been decided by a court.

Polymarket US and OG.com filed their own federal suits against Griffin on Nov. 9, [Spinner reported](https://askspinner.com/news/cftc-doj-sue-arkansas-griffin-kalshi).

*In our opinion: Washington is now a plaintiff in the state-versus-prediction-market fight, on top of the companies suing on their own. The stake is every CFTC-listed event contract sold in Arkansas, plus the brokers and apps that route them. The first thing to watch is whether the government files for a preliminary injunction, which the public docket does not yet show.*

articles.title: French Inflation Hits 3.7%, Highest Since 2023, as Energy Jumps 24%
articles.excerpt: INSEE trimmed its first estimate of 3.8%. Core inflation, which leaves out energy and fresh food, rose to 1.7% from 1.5% in September.
articles.body_md:
Consumer prices in France rose 3.7% in October from a year earlier on the EU's harmonised measure, statistics office INSEE said Friday, up from 3.4% in September. That's the [highest since December 2023](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-13/french-inflation-rises-to-3-7-in-october-highest-since-december-2023), Reuters reported, though it was a touch below the 3.8% first estimate.

Energy prices were up 24.1% on the year, [INSEE said](https://www.insee.fr/en/statistiques/9131375), the fourth straight month the pace has quickened. Gas alone rose 5.5% in October from September.

**Two measures, one country**

France publishes two inflation numbers. The national CPI rose 3.4%. The harmonised index (HICP) is built the same way in every euro zone country so they can be compared, and it gives more weight to some items. That weighting gap explains almost all of the 0.35-point difference this month, INSEE said. The HICP is the one the European Central Bank uses for its [2% target](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/mopo/strategy/html/index.en.html).

Core inflation, which leaves out volatile items such as energy and fresh food, rose to 1.7% from 1.5%. That is still below the ECB's 2% goal. Services inflation rose to 2.6% from 2.4%. Food went the other way, slowing to 1.2%.

On the month, prices rose 0.4% after a 0.3% fall in September, with transport services up 8.5%.

| Measure | October | September |
|---|---|---|
| HICP, year on year | 3.7% | 3.4% |
| CPI, year on year | 3.4% | 3.1% |
| Core | 1.7% | 1.5% |

France is the euro zone's second-largest economy. In crypto, bitcoin was near $69,250 at 5:57 a.m. ET, down 5.6% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $70,000 as Dollar Climbs to 19-Month High
articles.excerpt: More than $1.2 billion in leveraged crypto bets were force-closed in 24 hours, CoinGlass data show, and ether slipped under $2,000.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 late Thursday and was near $68,690 at 11:54 p.m. ET, down 6.8% in 24 hours, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show. That's its lowest level since August, according to [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/13/bitcoin-dips-below-usd70-000-as-selloff-gathers-pace) and [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/crypto-liquidations-bitcoin-ethereum-3-month-low/).

Ether fell 6.0% to about $1,927 over the same window, per CoinGecko.

**The dollar and bond yields kept climbing**

The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of major currencies, was near 103.16 on Thursday, its highest since April 2025, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/dollar-near-one-month-high-as-yen-edges-toward-160-.html). [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/8803914/dollar-rises-and-gold-sinks-as-t-note-yields-climb) also put it at a 1.5-year high. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.07%, CNBC said, after Tuesday's hotter-than-expected October inflation report lifted bets on a Fed rate hike in December.

When a Treasury note pays 5% with little risk, holding bitcoin, which pays nothing, costs more in lost income. A stronger dollar also makes dollar cash more attractive to hold. CoinDesk tied Thursday night's slide to the dollar's climb.

**$1.2 billion in forced selling**

A liquidation happens when an exchange closes a leveraged trade because the trader's losses have eaten through the cash posted as collateral. Those forced sales add selling just as prices fall.

More than $1.2 billion in crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours, CoinGlass data cited by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/13/bitcoin-dips-below-usd70-000-as-selloff-gathers-pace) and [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/bitcoin-price-crash-below-70000-nvidia-liquidations/) show. The largest single one was a bitcoin long (a bet on higher prices) worth about $31 million on Hyperliquid, a decentralized trading platform.

**Fund and stablecoin money kept leaving**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $47.7 million on Thursday, and ether ETFs lost $8.0 million, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data show. That follows the $1.44 billion that left bitcoin funds over five sessions, [Black Mint reported](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-etfs-five-straight-days-outflows/) Thursday.

Total stablecoin supply, the dollar tokens traders use to buy crypto, stood at $288.1 billion, down $5.02 billion in a week, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data show.

*In our opinion: this leg down started in the bond market. With CNBC citing a 91% chance of a December hike on CME FedWatch, Tuesday's hot inflation report pushed yields and the dollar higher. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and the weekly stablecoin count is the gauge of whether new cash is coming back on-chain.*

articles.title: Fed's Williams Says 'Work to Do' as Inflation Stays Too High
articles.excerpt: The New York Fed chief said the Fed can slow price rises but can't roll prices back. Futures put a December hike at about 91%, CNBC said.
articles.body_md:
New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday evening that inflation is "persistent" and the Fed will need to act "over time" to get it back to 2%, with its policy rate now at 3.75% to 4%.

"We still have work to do ... to get monetary policy to the right place," Williams said at a UC Berkeley alumni event in New York, [Reuters reported](https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/fed-s-williams-says-central-bank-has-work-to-do-to-get-inflation-back-on-target-ce785ed9d88cf324). He didn't say when the next increase would come or how large it would be. [A TMGM market note](https://www.tmg-max.com/en/analysis/market-news/article/feds-williams-inflation-remains-too-elevated-202611130020) of his remarks records the same message: inflation "too elevated" and an economy that is "resilient."

Williams carries extra weight. The New York Fed president is a permanent voting member of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee, under the [Fed's own rules](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm).

**The Fed can't lower the price level**

Asked about the cost of living, Williams said there's little the Fed can do about it. The Fed's tools work on the speed of price increases, not on the price level itself. Raising rates cools borrowing and spending so prices rise more slowly; it doesn't make last year's groceries cheaper.

Trying to "put the genie back in the bottle" by pushing prices down "creates huge distortions and damage to the economy," he said, according to Reuters.

**How big the next step is**

Futures traders put about a 91% chance on a December hike, CNBC [reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/dollar-near-one-month-high-as-yen-edges-toward-160-.html) from CME FedWatch data, after Tuesday's October consumer price report came in hotter than expected. Core prices rose 0.3% in the month, Reuters said.

Not every official wants big moves. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has argued for smaller, steady increases so the economy can adjust, according to Reuters and a [Babypips market recap](https://www.babypips.com/news/daily-financial-forex-market-recap-2026-11-12).

Bitcoin fell 6.8% in the 24 hours to 11:54 p.m. ET, to about $68,690, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show.

*In our opinion: anyone waiting for prices to slide back to 2019 levels just heard the Fed say that isn't on the menu. The live question is pace, a quarter point or a half, and Hammack's case for smaller steps is the counterweight to watch. The answer comes at the Dec. 8-9 meeting.*

articles.title: Illinois' 0.2% Crypto Tax Faces Brief From 18 Industry Groups
articles.excerpt: The groups say DeFi developers have no customers to collect from. The tax would hit each trade, transfer or custody of crypto for Illinois customers.
articles.body_md:
Eighteen crypto groups and companies, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Uniswap Labs and Chainlink Labs, asked an Illinois court to let them argue that the state's 0.2% Digital Asset Tax Act is unlawful, the [DeFi Education Fund said Thursday](https://www.defieducationfund.org/def-amici-submit-amicus-brief-illinois-digital-asset-tax-act-is-unlawful-and-unenforceable/).

The law reaches a lot of people. The brief estimates 2.64 million Illinois residents hold digital assets, the fifth-highest count of any state.

**How the tax works**

Under the Act, a broker that exchanges, transfers or holds crypto for an Illinois customer must collect 0.2% of the asset's value each time, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/18-crypto-firms-seek-to-join-court-fight-over-illinois-0-2-crypto-tax/) and [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383144/illinois-crypto-tax-draws-alliance-doj-banks-defi) reported. On a $10,000 transfer, that's $20. The levy is on the full value, so it applies whether or not the customer made money.

The statute sets a Jan. 1, 2027 start. Illinois agreed in October to push that to July 1, 2027, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-12-andreessen-horowitz-defi-education-fund-push-back-against-illinois-crypto-tax-438573) and Decrypt reported, though Unchained said it could not confirm a court approved the delay. None of the documents Black Mint reviewed estimate how much the tax would raise.

**The DeFi argument**

An amicus brief lets outsiders who aren't parties to a case give the court their view. This one, filed in Sangamon County, backs lawsuits from the Blockchain Association, the Crypto Council for Innovation, The Digital Chamber and the Illinois Blockchain Association.

The groups say the law's definitions are vague enough to cover decentralized finance, apps run by code rather than a company holding customer money. Developers of that software "have no customers to collect from, no assets to remit from, and no way to know where a transaction occurred," the brief says, as quoted by Unchained.

They also argue the tax singles out blockchain activity, since Illinois doesn't tax the same transfers of stocks, bonds or precious metals.

The plaintiffs don't oppose the filing, and Unchained found no order granting it. Neither Unchained nor The Block reported a response to the brief from Illinois officials.

*In our opinion: this case turns on one word, "broker." Read narrowly, the tax lands on exchanges and custodians that can actually collect it. Read broadly, it reaches software makers who never touch a customer's coins, which is why a16z and Uniswap Labs signed on. Watch for the court's ruling on the brief and whether the July 1, 2027 date holds.*

articles.title: US Gets Court Nod to Seize $1.2 Billion From Binance Hack Haul
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors can now seize or restrain $1.2 billion of the more than $2.7 billion frozen since the Oct. 29 hack. Binance says it has finished covering customers.
articles.body_md:
U.S. prosecutors have court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the crypto stolen from Binance on Oct. 29, the [Justice Department said Thursday](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-announces-actions-disrupt-north-koreas-massive-theft-cryptocurrency). More than $2.7 billion has been frozen so far by government and private-sector efforts.

The department again blamed the theft of more than $6 billion on North Korean military hackers the FBI calls TraderTraitor. North Korea rejected the [FBI's Oct. 31 finding](https://www.fbi.gov/investigate/cyber/alerts/2026/north-korea-responsible-for-6-billion-binance-attack), Black Mint [reported Nov. 2](https://blackmint.markets/news/north-korea-denies-fbi-binance-hack/), and had not publicly answered Thursday's announcement as of 6 p.m. ET.

**A freeze is not yet a seizure**

A freeze happens when an exchange or stablecoin issuer blocks an address or account so the coins can't move. A court-authorized seizure or restraint goes further: a judge lets the government take or hold the assets, which can lead to a civil forfeiture case and, eventually, a return to victims. About 44% of the frozen money has reached that court stage. Tracing continues as the hackers push funds through bridges, mixers and exchanges, the DOJ said.

**Binance says customer balances are whole**

Hours earlier, Binance said it "has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident," according to [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/binance-covers-6-34-billion-hack) and [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261113000200315). The exchange said it spent more than $6.34 billion of company money, drawing on its SAFU user-protection fund, part of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. A new proof-of-reserves snapshot covers 198 tokens; the cryptographic proof that lets users check their own balances will take about 40 to 50 hours, Binance said.

Covering customers is not the same as recovering the stolen coins: Binance bought replacement tokens on the market.

**A second scheme: fake video calls**

The DOJ also said it seized cloud servers behind FaceStealer, a North Korean campaign it tied to more than $400 million in crypto theft over 18 months. Attackers used hijacked accounts to set up video calls, played recordings or deepfakes of people the victims knew, then faked a technical glitch to get them to install malware, the department said.

*In our opinion: $1.2 billion in court hands is real progress, but it's less than a fifth of what was taken. The number to watch now is how much of the other $1.5 billion in frozen funds turns into forfeiture filings in Washington, D.C. FaceStealer is the sobering part: a familiar face on a video call is no longer proof of who is on the other end.*

articles.title: Trump Names Two Nominees Each for Short-Staffed SEC and CFTC
articles.excerpt: The CFTC has one commissioner and the SEC two. Four nominations sent Thursday would fill most of the empty seats if the Senate confirms them.
articles.body_md:
President Donald Trump sent four nominations to the Senate on Thursday, two each for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the [White House said](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/11/nominations-sent-to-the-senate-16a6/). The two agencies that split most U.S. crypto oversight now have three commissioners between them, out of 10 seats.

The picks, per the White House list:

- **Kristin N. Johnson** (SEC), for a term ending June 5, 2029, in the seat once held by Caroline Crenshaw. Johnson is a former CFTC commissioner, [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/12/u-s-president-names-cftc-sec-nominees-for-first-time-in-a-year).
- **Steven Levine** (SEC), for a term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Hester Peirce.
- **Nathan Anonick** (CFTC), for a term ending June 19, 2031, in the seat once held by Rostin Behnam.
- **Matthew Rowland** (CFTC), for the rest of a term ending April 13, 2028, replacing Summer Mersinger.

**Who's there now**

The [SEC's own page](https://www.sec.gov/about/sec-commissioners) lists just Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. The [CFTC's page](https://www.cftc.gov/About/Commissioners/index.htm) lists only Chairman Michael Selig, sworn in Dec. 22, 2025. Each agency is built for five members, with no more than three from one party, under rules both sites spell out.

That makes the CFTC a one-person commission today. Every commission vote, crypto rules included, runs through a single member. More commissioners mean more votes, more dissents on the record and a sturdier base for rules that may later face court challenges.

**What has to happen next**

Nominees go first to committee: Senate Agriculture for the CFTC picks and Senate Banking for the SEC picks, before a full Senate vote, CoinDesk reported. The Senate is in its post-election lame-duck session.

*In our opinion: an agency run by one commissioner can move fast, but its rules rest on a single signature, which is thin ground for markets that want rules to last past the next election. If confirmed, these four would take the two regulators from three members to seven. The next thing to watch is whether the Agriculture and Banking committees set hearing dates before the lame-duck session runs out.*

articles.title: Visa Lets Partners Settle in Western Union's USDPT via Anchorage
articles.excerpt: USDPT is the first Anchorage-issued stablecoin cleared for VisaNet settlement. Visa is also one of Anchorage's investors, the bank's own release says.
articles.body_md:
Visa and eligible partners can now pay what they owe each other on VisaNet using USDPT, Western Union's dollar stablecoin, [Anchorage Digital said](https://www.anchorage.com/press-room/anchorage-digital-to-support-visa-stablecoin-settlement-starting-with-usdpt) on Thursday. USDPT is the first of the six stablecoins Anchorage Digital Bank issues to get that status.

The bank issues and holds the token. Its other five include Tether's USAT, Ethena's USDtb and Zelle's ZLUSD, and the companies set up a framework to consider adding more after the USDPT launch.

**How card settlement works**

When you tap a Visa card, the shop gets paid quickly, but the banks behind the purchase square up later. Your card's issuing bank owes money to the shop's bank, and VisaNet tallies those debts and settles them, normally in ordinary dollars through banks. Settling in a stablecoin (a token meant to hold a steady $1 value) lets that money move on a blockchain at any hour.

Anchorage says each of its stablecoins is fully backed by U.S. dollars and cash equivalents and redeemable 1:1. Its bank is federally chartered and overseen by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

"Stablecoins have made money move faster, but speed alone won't bring institutions onchain," Anchorage CEO Nathan McCauley said in the release. Visa's Dan Roesbery, who runs its global crypto partnerships, said the deal gives partners "another trusted, institution-grade option."

**Who gets paid**

Neither company disclosed fees, volumes or which partners plan to use USDPT first. One tie worth knowing: Visa is listed among Anchorage's investors in the bank's own release, alongside Goldman Sachs, KKR and Andreessen Horowitz.

The deal lands while the stablecoin market shrinks. Total supply stood at $289.3 billion on Thursday, down $4.65 billion over the past week, [DefiLlama data](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) show. USDT accounts for $175.6 billion of it and USDC $69.7 billion.

*In our opinion: the stake is Visa's back office, the part of card payments most people never see. The next checkpoint is volume. Until Visa or Anchorage says how much USDPT actually settles, all anyone can count is the open door.*

This is not financial advice.

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Under $72,000 as Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resigns as CEO
articles.excerpt: Nvidia shares fell more than 12% early before trimming losses. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the 10-year Treasury yield is back above 5%.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell below $72,000 on Thursday, trading near $71,700 at 12 p.m. ET, down 3.4% over 24 hours, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show. It was the same morning Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive.

Ether did no better (near $2,006, down 3.3%).

**Nvidia names its CFO interim chief**

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, stepped down and will also leave the board, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-to-step-down-in-big-blow-to-ai-boom-5021980). Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board searches inside and outside the company for a permanent successor. Nvidia also named former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as its first board chair.

Nvidia's board met Wednesday to consider removing him after reports about his personal relationships, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Huang holds about 3.61% of the company, making him its fourth-largest shareholder.

Nvidia stock fell more than 12% in early trading, on course to erase about $500 billion of market value, before paring losses. By late morning it was down about 4%, while AMD gained 7% and Broadcom 5.4%, according to a [later Reuters market report](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4006089-global-markets-wall-street-edges-up-nvidia-drops-after-ceo-resigns). The S&P 500 was up 0.29% at that point.

**Why a bond yield matters here: the 5% line**

That same Reuters report said the 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5%. A Treasury yield is the interest the U.S. government pays to borrow. When it rises, a safe bond pays more, and assets that pay no interest at all, like bitcoin, have to compete harder for the same money.

No source has tied bitcoin's drop to Nvidia directly. Stocks steadied by late morning. Bitcoin had not.

*In our opinion: the number worth watching is that 5% yield. Stocks shook off a $500 billion scare by late morning, while bitcoin kept sliding. No source has explained that gap yet. The next Nvidia checkpoint is Kress's Nov. 18 employee meeting (Reuters reported the date), and the next bitcoin one is whether the 10-year holds above 5%.*

articles.title: DTCC Plans to Bring Tokenized Stocks and Treasuries to Solana in 2027
articles.excerpt: The firm that holds $114 trillion of securities launched its tokenization service Oct. 28. Solana tokens would keep the same investor protections, DTCC says.
articles.body_md:
The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation said Thursday it plans to let eligible securities held at its depository be turned into tokens on Solana, with the link expected in the second half of 2027, according to [DTCC's announcement](https://www.dtcc.com/press-releases/2026/dtcc-tokenization-service-to-connect-with-solana).

That is a big name for any blockchain to land. DTCC sits underneath most U.S. stock trading. Its depository arm, The Depository Trust Company (DTC), held securities from more than 150 countries worth $114 trillion in 2025, and its subsidiaries processed $4.7 quadrillion of transactions that year, the company says.

**How a DTC token works**

Today, when you own a share through a broker, the real record of ownership sits at DTC. Tokenization creates a digital copy of that position on a blockchain (a shared ledger that records transfers around the clock). The DTCC Tokenization Service, which went live Oct. 28, does this for eligible assets that member firms choose to convert, while the underlying security stays in DTC's custody.

DTCC says the tokens will carry "the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards" as traditionally held securities, in the words of Brian Steele, president of its clearing and securities business. That sets them apart from synthetic stock tokens, which track a share's price without giving holders the share itself.

The [Solana Foundation's post](https://solana.com/news/dtcc-tokenization-service-to-connect-with-solana) says the integration will support converting eligible assets into tokens and the full token lifecycle once it connects.

**What isn't known yet**

Neither announcement says which securities will be offered on Solana first, how much is expected to move there, or what DTCC will charge firms to use it. The plan is a target date, not a launch.

*In our opinion: Wall Street's plumbing is picking blockchains the way a broker picks trading venues, by where the customers already are. The question worth chasing is volume, and DTCC hasn't put a number on that. The calendar says second half of 2027, which in crypto years is roughly forever, so the next checkpoint is which firms sign up to use the Solana link.*

This is not financial advice.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $1.44 Billion Over Five Straight Days of Outflows
articles.excerpt: BlackRock's IBIT lost $269.7 million on Wednesday alone. Morgan Stanley's MSBT was the only fund to take money in, adding $9.0 million.
articles.body_md:
Investors pulled $299.8 million out of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Wednesday, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data show. It was the fifth straight trading day of net outflows, and the five days add up to about $1.44 billion.

[Black Mint reported](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-lowest-since-august-etf-outflows/) Nov. 10 that the first three days of the streak had cost the funds about $1.04 billion. Tuesday added $95.0 million in outflows. Wednesday's figure was more than three times that.

**BlackRock's IBIT did most of the selling**

IBIT, the biggest fund, lost $269.7 million on Wednesday, and Grayscale's GBTC lost $39.1 million. Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in $9.0 million, the only fund with net inflows that day. MSBT also took in $22.1 million on Monday and $20.0 million on Tuesday, the same table shows.

Ether funds lost money on Wednesday as well, $144.8 million, with BlackRock's ETHA accounting for $129.8 million, Farside's [ether table](https://farside.co.uk/ethereum-etf-flow-all-data/) shows.

**How a flow becomes a sale**

A flow measures cash moving in or out; the price is a separate thing. When more holders cash out of a spot ETF than buy in, the large trading firms that make markets in it hand shares back to the issuer, and the issuer delivers or sells the matching bitcoin. So an outflow day means coins leaving the funds' custody accounts.

Size matters here. Even after this streak, the U.S. funds have taken in a net $55.17 billion since they launched in January 2024, by Farside's running total. November has been harder: about $1.88 billion out across eight trading days, with Nov. 4 the only day of net inflows ($74.6 million).

Bitcoin was near $73,390 at 6:02 a.m. ET Thursday, down 0.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). The Crypto Fear & Greed Index sat at 28, in "fear," per [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/).

*In our opinion: the funds are still about $55 billion ahead since launch, so the streak has dented the pile without emptying it. The detail worth following is MSBT, which kept collecting money on three days when IBIT was handing it back. Thursday's flow numbers will show whether the streak reaches six. Five red days in a row is not the kind of streak anyone frames for the office wall.*

articles.title: India's Retail Inflation Breaks the RBI's Ceiling, Rising to 6.09%
articles.excerpt: Food prices rose 8.94% from a year earlier, and economists polled by Reuters had expected 5.93%. The RBI's next rate decision is Dec. 4.
articles.body_md:
India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, government data showed Thursday, above the 6% upper limit of the Reserve Bank of India's tolerance band. It was 5.54% in September.

The reading lands three weeks before the RBI's next policy decision on Dec. 4, and it is the last inflation print the central bank will see before then, [Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/economy/retail-inflation-jumps-to-6-09-in-october-14078348.html) and [News18](https://www.news18.com/business/economy/indias-cpi-inflation-jumps-to-6-09-in-october-breaches-rbis-upper-tolerance-band-10423184.html) reported.

**Food did the heavy lifting**

Food prices rose 8.94% from a year earlier, by the government's consumer food price index, up from about 7.7% in September, the [Ministry of Statistics](https://www.mospi.gov.in/themes/product/9-consumer-price-index-cpi) figures show. Rural inflation was 6.63% and urban inflation 5.41%, the ministry said in its release, as quoted by News18. All figures are provisional.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected 5.93%, with forecasts from 5.50% to 6.60%, [The Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/indicators/indias-october-retail-inflation-quickens-to-6-09-to-breach-rbis-tolerance-ceiling-food-fuel-cost/articleshow/135763003.cms) reported, carrying Reuters' story. Onion prices have nearly doubled since January, and food makes up nearly 40% of the index, according to that report.

**How India's inflation target works**

The consumer price index tracks what households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. India now measures it against a 2024 base year, a change made on Feb. 12, 2026. The RBI aims for 4% inflation and treats anything from 2% to 6% as tolerable. When prices run above that band, the bank can raise its repo rate (what it charges commercial banks to borrow), which pushes up borrowing costs across the economy.

The RBI started raising rates in October. Economists in an earlier Reuters poll expected another 25 basis point increase in December, to 5.75%. Upasna Bhardwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, expects 50 more basis points of hikes in the fiscal year that ends in March 2027, according to comments carried by News18.

*In our opinion: the date that matters now is Dec. 4. October came in 0.16 percentage points above the Reuters median, and food, the biggest slice of the basket, is running near 9%, so the RBI has little room to wait. For crypto readers, India is one more large economy where borrowing costs are going up this winter.*

articles.title: Russia Clears Crypto Exchange Trading, Pending Central Bank Sign-Off
articles.excerpt: Retail buyers will be limited to bitcoin, ether and USDT, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary, from Nov. 17. Moscow Exchange targets Dec. 1.
articles.body_md:
Russian exchanges may start organized crypto trading from Nov. 22, the [Bank of Russia](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/event/?id=32975) said Wednesday, but only after the central bank agrees to each venue's trading rules. The Justice Ministry has registered the ordinance that sets the requirements.

The central bank's notice doesn't say whether any exchange has cleared that review yet.

**What exchanges have to do**

Under the ordinance, an exchange must register everyone who trades through it, such as brokers, trust managers and central counterparties (the clearing firms that stand between buyer and seller). It must keep registers of orders and deals, monitor trading and publish current, weighted-average, market and closing prices. It reports results to the central bank the same way it already does for stocks and bonds, the notice says. Russian news site [Lenta.ru](https://lenta.ru/news/2026/11/11/bank-rossii-dal-ukazanie-po-zapusku-torgov-kriptovalyutami/) reported the same terms.

**Retail buyers get three coins and a cap**

A separate ordinance, announced Nov. 6 and taking effect Nov. 17, lists what ordinary investors can buy: bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT, [the Bank of Russia said](https://www.cbr.ru/press/event/?id=32966). They can buy through brokers, trust managers or registered crypto exchange offices, up to 300,000 rubles a year through any one intermediary. Qualified investors face no list and no cap. Everyone has to pass a test and read a risk disclosure first.

The central bank said it picked the three by market value, average daily volume and at least five years of price history on foreign exchanges. Using crypto to pay for goods and services inside Russia remains banned, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/russia-clears-exchange-crypto-trading) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/russian-exchanges-crypto-trading-november-22/) reported.

**Moscow Exchange is aiming for Dec. 1**

Moscow Exchange, the country's largest trading venue, plans a pilot for bitcoin, ether and USDT trading from Dec. 1, both outlets reported. The U.S. Treasury [sanctioned](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2404) Moscow Exchange and its clearing house in June 2024. The legal base is Federal Law No. 282-FZ on digital currencies, in force since Sept. 1, according to Lenta.ru.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is which exchange gets its rules approved first, and whether that happens before Moscow Exchange's Dec. 1 pilot. A 300,000-ruble yearly cap per intermediary keeps retail buying small by design. Watch Nov. 17, when the three-coin list takes effect.*

articles.title: Zcash Holders to Vote on Pulling 50,000 ZEC From Its Grants Treasury
articles.excerpt: The plan would also end Zcash Community Grants' 8% cut of new coins and lock it in a fund nobody can spend from yet. Polls close Nov. 30.
articles.body_md:
Zcash coinholders start voting Nov. 16 on a plan to take 50,000 ZEC, about $49.5 million at Thursday's price, out of the treasury of Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the network's grants program. The coins would come out of circulation and return to miners over time.

The draft proposal, written by Zcash co-founders Sean Bowe and Zooko Wilcox with Jason McGee of Shielded Labs, was [merged](https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1428) into the Zcash specifications repository late Tuesday ET. Polls for coinholders and community panels run through Nov. 30, [BlockchainReporter](https://blockchainreporter.net/zcash-50000-zec-dev-fund-vote/) reported.

**Two changes, one vote**

The [proposal](https://zips.z.cash/draft-mcgee-future-dev-legal-defense-fund) does two things. First, ZCG would stop receiving its 8% slice of newly mined coins. Until the third halving, that 8% would flow into a new lockbox called the Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund, and nobody could spend from it until a later proposal sets the rules.

Second, ZCG would have 30 days after activation to remove 50,000 ZEC from circulation. That is about 55% of the 91,452.98 ZEC on its dashboard in late October, the draft says.

**How the mining reserve works**

Zcash pays miners a subsidy per block that halves on a set schedule. The Network Sustainability Mechanism, switched on in the recent NU7 upgrade, collects removed coins and pays them back out as future block rewards, so miners have income as the subsidy shrinks.

The 8% stream works out to about 144 ZEC a day, or 52,560 a year, by the draft's math. At an assumed $1,300 per ZEC and 2026 spending levels, ZCG's treasury covers about 13 years of grants now and about six after the removal. The draft notes its dashboard figures "have not been independently reconciled."

A poll doesn't move coins. The change needs rough consensus and a follow-up network upgrade, NU7.1, with no activation height set yet. The separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund is untouched.

ZEC was near $991 at 6:05 a.m. ET, up 0.8% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/zcash).

*In our opinion: the number to watch is the Nov. 30 poll result, then whether miners and engineers can agree on an NU7.1 date. The proposal shrinks ZCG's runway from about 13 years to about six on its own assumptions, at a lower price today than the $1,300 it uses. Who spends from the new lockbox, and how, is still unwritten.*

articles.title: MSCI Drops Strategy From Its Global Indexes, Effective After Nov. 30
articles.excerpt: Metaplanet and uranium holder Yellow Cake are also out. J.P. Morgan had put possible outflows from Strategy stock at up to $8.8 billion if others follow.
articles.body_md:
Strategy is coming out of MSCI's flagship stock indexes. The index provider will delete the bitcoin-holding company from the MSCI USA Index at the Nov. 30 close, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/msci-to-drop-strategy-from-global-indexes-putting-billions-in-passive-fund-inflows-at-risk-5020015) Wednesday, after deciding that companies like it look more like investment funds than operating businesses.

Index funds don't get a say in this. A fund that tracks an MSCI benchmark has to hold what's in it and sell what leaves, so a deleted stock loses a built-in group of buyers. J.P. Morgan had estimated that outflows from Strategy stock could reach $8.8 billion if other index providers follow MSCI, Reuters reported.

**Metaplanet and Yellow Cake are out too**

MSCI's November review deletes 100 securities from the MSCI ACWI Index, its all-country benchmark, with every change taking effect as of the Nov. 30 close, its [announcement](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?format=html&lang=en&pub_key=t6TJpGLKQvg%3D) shows. Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, another bitcoin buyer, leaves the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index, and UK uranium holder Yellow Cake is also on the deletion list, according to Reuters and [Blockhead](https://www.blockhead.co/2026/11/12/msci-deletes-strategy-and-metaplanet-from-its-indexes/). Ether treasury company SharpLink landed on MSCI's watchlist instead.

Strategy's shares fell about 2.5% in extended trading on Wednesday.

**How MSCI's new test works**

This is the first review under MSCI's rule for what it calls non-operating companies. A company first has to show that more than half of its assets are operating assets; if it can't, it faces five financial measures. A company already in an index is removed only after failing that screen in its two most recent annual filing periods, Blockhead and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-11-11-strategy-metaplanet-lose-msci-index-membership-november-reshuffle-438437) reported. MSCI's review documents gave no company-specific reasons.

**Strategy argued against the rule**

Strategy, Metaplanet and Yellow Cake did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. In a letter to MSCI earlier this year, Strategy said deletion would do little to its business, Blockhead and The Block reported. Leaving an index doesn't require Strategy to sell any bitcoin.

Bitcoin was near $73,680 at 11:59 p.m. ET Wednesday, roughly flat over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the date to circle is Nov. 30, when tracking funds have to finish selling. Strategy says the exit will do little to its business, and J.P. Morgan's $8.8 billion figure depends on other index makers copying MSCI, so the next provider to rule on treasury companies is the real test. Being called a fund by the people who build funds is an odd sort of compliment.*

articles.title: Japan's Producer Prices Rise 7.1% as Fuel and Metals Costs Climb
articles.excerpt: October's reading beat forecasts by 0.6 point and tops September's 6.8%. Copper-linked metals rose 31.7%, as the BOJ weighs its 1.25% rate.
articles.body_md:
Japanese companies paid 7.1% more for goods in October than a year earlier, up from 6.8% in September, the [Bank of Japan said](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/statistics/pi/cgpi_release/cgpi2610.pdf) Thursday. That beat the private-sector forecast by 0.6 percentage point, [Nikkei reported](https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUB1166J0R11C26A1000000/).

The figure came out at 8:50 a.m. Tokyo time, or 6:50 p.m. ET Wednesday. It lands on a central bank that held its policy rate at 1.25% last month, with one board member voting for 1.5%, its [October statement](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030a.pdf) shows.

**What this index tracks**

The corporate goods price index measures what companies charge each other for goods, from steel to fuel, before anything reaches a store. It's read as an early guide to consumer prices, since business costs tend to show up on shelves later, as [Sankei](https://www.sankei.com/article/20261112-3AAWJRVFWZOUTG6YZISIUXGP5U/) and Nikkei noted. Prices rose 0.7% from September alone.

**Fuel, chemicals and metals led**

The BOJ release and both newspapers show:
- Petroleum and coal products: up 15.9% from a year earlier
- Chemicals: up 15.5%
- Nonferrous metals, including copper: up 31.7%
- Farm, forestry and fishery products: down 25.0%

Import prices in yen were 24.8% higher than a year ago. Nikkei tied the fuel rise to higher crude prices since the summer, and the copper gain to demand from data centers.

**Why a Tokyo price report reaches crypto**

A BOJ rate hike makes it more expensive to borrow in yen, including for investors outside Japan who fund trades in other assets with yen. The board's next policy meeting is Dec. 17-18, per its [meeting calendar](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

Bitcoin was near $73,680 at 11:59 p.m. ET Wednesday, roughly flat over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the gap worth watching is 7.1% wholesale inflation against a 1.25% policy rate, with one vote for a hike already on the record in October. Companies are eating higher fuel and metal costs now. How much of that reaches shoppers in Japan's next consumer price report is the question the board carries into Dec. 17.*

articles.title: Aave Risk Adviser Proposes Freezing $1.33 Billion of Core Collateral
articles.excerpt: StakeWise's founder asked for a separate vote on osETH, where $279.4 million of collateral backs loans at about 14 times leverage.
articles.body_md:
Aave's risk adviser LlamaRisk wants to freeze nine more tokens on Aave V3 Core, the lending app's main Ethereum market, in a plan covering $1.33 billion of collateral backing $1.03 billion of loans as of Nov. 9. On Wednesday, one issuer asked for its own vote.

LlamaRisk, which is funded in part by the Aave DAO, posted the [proposal](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-repositioning-aave-v3-core-around-established-liquid-collateral/26191) on Aave's governance forum on Nov. 10.

**How a freeze works**

On Aave, users deposit tokens and borrow against them. A freeze blocks new deposits and new borrowing against a token and sets its loan-to-value ratio (the share of a deposit's value a user can borrow) to zero. Existing loans stay open and can be repaid or moved at any time. On frozen reserves still carrying more than $20,000 of debt, the DAO's cut of interest would rise to 99%. LlamaRisk said borrow rates wouldn't change.

**Most of the money sits in ether loops**

Two of the five big tokens are already frozen: Kelp DAO's rsETH since April and Threshold's tBTC since Oct. 31. The new freezes would hit StakeWise's osETH ($279.4 million of collateral backing $256.6 million of debt), Lombard's LBTC ($177.4 million and $72.1 million) and Rocket Pool's rETH ($81.8 million and $35.4 million).

The osETH loans run at about 14 times leverage: deposit staked ether, borrow ether, stake it, repeat.

The debt in scope earns the DAO about $3.7 million a year, LlamaRisk said. If exposure doesn't shrink, the plan allows small, monthly cuts to liquidation thresholds and, as a last step, a WETH borrow-rate rise of up to 1 percentage point. "We will not make abrupt parameter changes that would liquidate significant positions," LlamaRisk wrote.

**StakeWise asks for a separate vote**

A post signed by StakeWise founder Dmitri asked LlamaRisk and the DAO on Nov. 11 to "move the proposed osETH freeze to a separate vote." Lombard and Rocket Pool hadn't posted in the thread by Wednesday evening. No vote had been posted to Snapshot as of Nov. 11, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/llamarisk-asks-aave-to-freeze-stakewise-lombard-and-rocket-pool-tokens-on-its-v3-core-market/) reported.

*In our opinion: the number to watch is $862 million, the WETH debt tied to the rsETH and osETH loops, because that's where any rate change would land. Aave is asking those borrowers to leave, politely and on their own schedule. The first real test is whether the DAO splits osETH out, as StakeWise asked, before anything reaches a vote.*

articles.title: South Korean Lawmakers Tentatively Back Crypto Tax Delay to 2029
articles.excerpt: The bill hasn't passed. Lawmakers still split over making exchanges hand trading records to the tax office from 2027, two years before any tax is due.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's ruling and main opposition parties tentatively agreed on Wednesday to push the country's crypto income tax back two years, to 2029, [Yonhap reported](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261111011000320). The tax is set to start in January 2027 under current law.

Black Mint [reported Nov. 6](https://blackmint.markets/news/south-korea-crypto-tax-2029/) that the government would seek the delay. This is the first sign the National Assembly will go along.

**No vote yet**

Rep. Oh Gi-hyoung of the ruling Democratic Party, who chairs the tax subcommittee, told reporters the parties found no real differences on the government's two-year plan, per [Yonhap's Korean report](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261111170100001). The subcommittee did not pass the bill. Oh said the final vote will come on its last day of review.

Rep. Bae June-young of the opposition People Power Party said the government has to prepare responsibly if it delays again, and that lawmakers would check its progress, Yonhap reported.

The tax was first set for 2022. It was pushed to 2023, then 2025, then 2027, so this would be its fourth delay.

**What the bill changes**

The bill, filed by Democratic Party Rep. Ahn Do-geol from the finance ministry's plan, adds a three-year loss carryforward, [Edaily reported](https://www.edaily.co.kr/News/Read?newsId=03663766645644736). The idea: a losing year could reduce tax owed on gains in the next three years. Today only same-year losses count.

It would also make domestic exchanges send customers' trading records to the National Tax Service from 2027. Crypto moves between exchanges and overseas platforms, so the tax office says it needs the records to work out what each person paid and gained. The agency told Edaily it would use the data only to build a pre-filled filing system before the tax starts, not to tax anyone.

**Two points still open**

Lawmakers still disagree on that 2027 start date for exchange records, and the government opposes raising the tax-free allowance, Yonhap reported. Under current law, individuals would pay 22%, including local tax, on yearly crypto gains above 2.5 million won, [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10927485) reported last week.

*In our opinion: a tax first written for 2022 is heading for its fourth delay, and Korea's crypto traders get two more years without it. The detail worth chasing is the records rule, because exchanges could be filing customers' trades with the tax office in 2027, two years before anyone owes a won. The subcommittee's last session settles both questions.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Details Three Fixed Bugs, One That Could Stall Miners
articles.excerpt: The worst flaw left some mining nodes unable to build blocks after a reorg. Fixes shipped in 30.0 and 29.2 in October 2025; 29.x hit end of life Oct. 27.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin Core published details of three security bugs on Nov. 10, including a High-severity flaw that left some mining nodes unable to build blocks after a reorg. All three were fixed more than a year ago.

Anyone still running an old node is the one with the stake here. The fixes shipped in Bitcoin Core 30.0 on Oct. 10, 2025, and in 29.2 on Oct. 14, 2025, according to the project's [advisories](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/). The project waited until the last vulnerable release line, 29.x, reached end of life on Oct. 27, 2026, before publishing the details. None of the three write-ups says whether a bug was ever exploited.

**How a reorg jammed a miner's block template**

A node keeps a mempool, its waiting room for unconfirmed transactions. Version 3 transactions, called TRUC (defined in BIP 431), may have only one unconfirmed parent and one unconfirmed child. Version 28.0 added "sibling eviction," which swaps an existing child for a better-paying one.

During a chain reorganization, when a node drops recent blocks for a competing chain, it puts their transactions back into the mempool. The [High-severity advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62861/) (CVE-2025-62861) says sibling eviction kept running during that step. That step evicted restored transactions in some cases, leaving the mempool inconsistent, so a miner's block template failed until the node was restarted. Versions 28.0 to 28.2 and 29.0 to 29.1 were affected.

**Two Medium-rated bugs**

The [second flaw](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62860/) only hit nodes using the optional -whitelist setting, which relaxes limits for trusted peers. Inbound Tor peers show up with the local Tor daemon's address, so whitelisting that range trusted every Tor peer. The advisory says vendor setups led to "thousands of reachable mainnet nodes whitelisting all incoming Tor connections."

The [third](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62859/) let a malicious peer stall block processing through compact blocks, a bandwidth-saving way to relay new blocks. If the attacker controlled all three of a node's high-bandwidth peers, or the node ran -blocksonly, the stall repeated with no end, the advisory says.

[Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/bitcoin-core-discloses-bugs-that-could-freeze-mining-nodes/) noted these are separate from three bugs the project disclosed on Oct. 28.

*In our opinion: the date to circle is Oct. 27. Once 29.x stopped getting updates, every node still on 28.x or 29.1 and older is running software with publicly documented flaws. Miners and node-in-a-box vendors carry most of that risk, and the fix has been sitting on the download page for 13 months.*

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Switches On Custody for Bitcoin, Ether and Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: Germany's largest lender now holds private keys for institutional clients in Europe, and it signed a digital-asset deal with its own money manager.
articles.body_md:
Deutsche Bank said on Wednesday that its digital asset custody service is live for paying clients, holding 5 tokens for institutions in Europe, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/deutsche-bank-launches-digital-asset-custody-service). It announced the plan in September.

The bank's [product page](https://digitalassets.db.com/) lists them: bitcoin, ether and the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins. It is for institutional investors, companies, governments and wealth managers, not retail customers.

**What custody means here**

Owning crypto comes down to controlling a private key, the secret code that moves coins. A custodian holds those keys for the client. Deutsche Bank says it stores them in hardware security modules (tamper-resistant key vaults), offers warm and cold storage, and lets clients set their own approval steps for transfers. Clients reach it through the bank's Autobahn gateway or its Corporate Bank portal.

The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and offered across Europe through passporting, and the bank describes it as compliant with the EU's MiCA crypto rules. For now it offers custody, transfers to other parties, and moves between warm and cold storage. "Further capabilities" are planned, the page says.

**A second deal inside the family**

The bank also signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the money manager it mostly owns that was until recently called DWS, Reuters reported. The two will explore commercial and technical work together in digital assets, the bank said, without naming products.

"In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets," Paul Maley, the bank's global head of trust and securities services, said, per Reuters.

**What the bank didn't say**

It didn't name its first clients, say how many signed up, or publish its fees, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/deutsche-bank-bitcoin-custody-live) noted. Crypto held this way also isn't covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme, the outlet said, citing the bank's September release.

*In our opinion: Germany's biggest bank opened the vault with a short menu of five tokens. The asset-management deal is the part to follow, because it keeps any new digital product inside one banking group. The bank has also told Reuters it wants to take custody to Asia. The first number worth asking for is the client count, which the bank has kept to itself so far.*

articles.title: Bitmine Reports $6.3 Billion Annual Loss, Nearly All From Ether's Drop
articles.excerpt: Revenue rose to $124.8 million, 97% of it from staking. The 10-K also says Bitmine is still fixing material weaknesses in its internal controls.
articles.body_md:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies lost $6.31 billion in the fiscal year that ended Aug. 31, its annual report filed Tuesday evening shows. Of that, $6.23 billion was an unrealized loss on its ether.

A year earlier, the company had net income of $348.6 million, according to the [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1829311/000162828026072846/bmnr-20260831.htm). The swing tracks the ether price, not the business.

**Why a falling token shows up as a loss**

Bitmine marks its crypto at fair value, meaning the market price on the reporting date, and books any change straight into profit. "Unrealized" means it didn't sell. If ether falls, the loss appears on the income statement anyway. If it rises, so does reported profit. The filing warns that this will keep causing "significant volatility" in results.

On Aug. 31 the company held 5,901,837 ETH worth $14.56 billion, about 4.9% of circulating supply, plus 211 bitcoin worth $16.6 million.

**Staking now pays most of the bills**

Revenue rose to $124.8 million from $6.1 million. Staking and validation brought in $121.4 million, or 97% of the total. Staking means locking ether to help run the Ethereum network in exchange for rewards, which Bitmine puts at about 2.5% to 4.0% a year, paid in ETH. When ether falls, those rewards are worth less in dollars.

**Follow the money**

Shareholders paid for the stack. Bitmine sold 395.1 million new shares through an at-the-market program, which lets a company sell stock gradually into the market, raising $13.2 billion before costs. It also bought back and retired 20.8 million shares for $353.8 million.

The 10-K also says the company is still working to fix material weaknesses in its internal control over financial reporting.

The buying hasn't stopped. As of Nov. 8, Bitmine held 6,070,092 ETH, or 4.97% of supply, its [Nov. 9 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1829311/000149315226050647/ex99-1.htm) said. Chairman Tom Lee has set 5% as the stopping point. Ether traded near $2,059 at 5:55 a.m. ET Wednesday, down 1.4% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the loss is on paper, but the shares sold to fund the buying are real, and 395 million of them now split whatever the ether is worth. The release valued the stack at $2,234 per ETH on Nov. 8; Wednesday's price is about 8% lower. The next markers are the 5% line, roughly 40,000 ETH away, and whether the next filing reports those control weaknesses fixed.*

articles.title: FSB Tells Türkiye It Needs a Stablecoin Regime in Crypto Peer Review
articles.excerpt: Türkiye has 7.1 million crypto accounts but no rules written for stablecoins. The FSB's peer review also flags slow bank custody licensing.
articles.body_md:
Türkiye should set up a dedicated rulebook for stablecoins, the Financial Stability Board said Wednesday in a [peer review](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/Peer-Review-of-Turkiye.pdf) of a crypto market that handled nearly $200 billion in transactions in 2025.

The FSB is the Basel-based group that coordinates financial rules for the G20. In 2023 it finished a global framework for crypto and stablecoins, and its members agreed to be checked against it. Türkiye volunteered for this review.

**Where Türkiye stands**

The [review](https://www.fsb.org/2026/11/peer-review-of-turkiye/) says Turkish authorities have made real progress since 2025. Crypto service providers must now register and get licensed by the Capital Markets Board (CMB). Crypto can't be used for domestic payments, and platforms may keep no more than 5% of client crypto in their own wallets. The rest sits with a separate custodian.

The size, per the report:

- more than 7.1 million crypto accounts, though only 51% hold a balance
- about $3 billion of holdings at licensed local providers, per official data cited in the report
- about $0.5 billion in daily crypto trading, against $3.9 billion on Borsa Istanbul

Bitcoin, ether, XRP and USDT make up more than 45% of local holdings.

**The stablecoin gap**

A stablecoin is a token pegged to a currency such as the dollar and backed by reserves. Türkiye treats them like any other crypto asset, the report says, so there are no specific rules on reserves or redemption, the main protections when a coin loses its peg. Some payment-type coins may fall under e-money rules instead.

The report says many users buy dollar stablecoins, mainly USDT, either to hedge against a weaker lira or to move money to foreign platforms. The only lira stablecoin from a local issuer, BiLira, has a market value of about $5.9 million.

The FSB also asks for a financial-stability monitoring framework, tougher supervision and enforcement, and more cross-border information sharing. Bank custody licensing has taken around 12 to 18 months, the report says, and industry firms quoted in it said no licensed bank had yet started offering custody.

*In our opinion: the hole the FSB found is the one that matters most to ordinary users, since a lira holder buying USDT is trusting reserves that no Turkish rule addresses. The report doesn't set a deadline, so the next thing to look for is a draft stablecoin law from Ankara and the first bank actually opening a custody desk.*

articles.title: Kraken's xStocks Adds 200-Plus UK and EU Stock Tokens, Passing 1,500
articles.excerpt: The tokens are backed 1:1 by shares, but holders get no voting rights, and UK and U.S. investors still can't buy them. Hong Kong stocks are next.
articles.body_md:
Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, put more than 200 tokenized UK and European Union stocks on its xStocks platform Wednesday, taking the lineup past 1,500 assets, the company [announced](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261111700594/en/xStocks-Broadens-Suite-of-Tokenized-Assets-Bringing-Hundreds-of-UK-and-EU-Listed-Equities-Onchain).

British investors are still shut out. The new tokens track UK shares, yet xStocks still can't be sold to investors in the UK, or to U.S. persons, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-11-kraken-parent-payward-adds-200-tokenized-uk-and-european-equities-to-xstocks-offering-437837) from the release.

**How a stock token works**

Each xStock is backed one-for-one: when a token is issued, a real share is bought and held at a regulated custodian for as long as the token trades. The first batch includes LVMH, Rolls-Royce and SAP, [The Defiant reported](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/xstocks-adds-200-plus-uk-and-eu-stock-tokens-with-gtn). GTN, a brokerage technology firm, handles the buying and custody for the new markets. The tokens then trade on Kraken, on partner venues and on blockchains including Solana, Ethereum and TON.

Legally, it isn't the share. xStocks are tracker certificates issued by Backed Assets (JE) Limited in Jersey, which give price exposure but no shareholder voting rights, the [xStocks legal overview](https://docs.xstocks.fi/docs/product-legal-overview) says. Kraken's [risk disclosure](https://www.kraken.com/legal/xstocks) adds that holders have no claim on the company's assets in a liquidation and pay fees set out in the prospectus, so returns won't match owning the stock.

**The size so far**

- more than $1.1 billion in assets under management
- more than $45 billion in total trading volume
- more than 550,000 holders
- available in more than 110 markets

Those holder numbers compare with more than 200,000 in September, The Block reported. Payward says hundreds of Hong Kong-listed stocks will follow within weeks. The London Stock Exchange, which partnered with Payward in September, plans to list xStocks on its LSE 24 venue in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

This is not financial advice.

*In our opinion: Rolls-Royce now comes as a token in more than 110 markets, just not in the UK, where it's based. Holder numbers more than doubled since September, so the platform is growing, but on $1.1 billion it's still small next to the markets it tracks. The clock to watch is the LSE 24 approval, the point where a British exchange itself starts listing the tokens.*

articles.title: Fed's Paulson Says 'Further Gradual Tightening Seems Appropriate'
articles.excerpt: Paulson listed three things that would make her move faster and said she isn't seeing them yet. Goolsbee called October CPI "borderline disturbing."
articles.body_md:
Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said Tuesday evening, Nov. 10, that "further gradual tightening seems appropriate," in [prepared remarks](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/the-economy/monetary-policy/261110-81st-annual-field-meeting-capstone-speech) delivered the same day consumer prices were reported up 0.4% for October.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told [PBS NewsHour](https://www.pbs.org/video/rising-prices-1794349770/) that report was "borderline disturbing." The Fed's next decision is due at its [Dec. 8-9 meeting](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm).

For crypto holders, the stake is the price of money. Higher policy rates lift what cash and Treasuries pay, which raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin.

**Paulson named three triggers for moving faster**

Paulson said she backed the Fed's September increase and its October hold. "Skipping a meeting is a matter of pace, not direction," she said. She prefers small steps so families, businesses and community banks can adjust to higher borrowing costs.

She would act more quickly if inflation expectations drift up, wage pressures build or underlying inflation moves higher. "Right now, that's not what I'm seeing," she said, adding that long-term expectations are well anchored.

**Goolsbee pointed to services and the AI build-out**

Goolsbee said the most troubling part of the report was services inflation, which he said is "not coming down" and is probably not mostly driven by oil or tariffs. He also tied some cost pressure to demand from the data-center build-out for AI. Asked by PBS host Geoff Bennett about Governor Christopher Waller's openness to a half-point December increase, he didn't commit. "Everything is always on the table," he said.

How the tool works: the Fed sets a target for the federal funds rate, what banks charge each other for overnight loans. Raising it pushes up borrowing costs across the economy, which is meant to slow spending and, in time, prices. Services prices get close attention because they follow wages and local demand more than one-off shocks such as an oil spike.

Bitcoin was near $73,680 at 11:54 p.m. ET Tuesday, down 1.3% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the argument inside the Fed has moved from whether to raise rates to how fast. Paulson listed exactly what would make her hurry, and she said she isn't seeing any of it yet. That makes wage data and inflation-expectation surveys the numbers to check before Dec. 9, when the decision lands.*

articles.title: Tron Inc. Profit Rises 22% to $14.9 Million as Per-Share Earnings Fall
articles.excerpt: Earnings per share fell to 3 cents from 11 cents as the share count more than quadrupled. The toy business lost money; the profit came from TRX gains and staking.
articles.body_md:
Tron Inc., a Nasdaq-listed toy maker that now holds most of its value in TRX tokens, said Tuesday its third-quarter net income rose 22% to $14.9 million. Basic earnings per share fell to 3 cents from 11 cents.

The gap comes from share count. The company averaged 474.4 million basic shares in the quarter, up from 110 million a year earlier, its [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1956744/000149315226050474/form10-q.htm) shows. Profit grew, but it was split among more than four times as many shares. On a diluted basis, which counts shares that could still be issued, EPS slipped to 3 cents from 4 cents.

**Where the profit came from**

None of it came from toys. The theme-park merchandise business grew sales to $1.19 million from $1.10 million but still lost $573,354 at the operating level. The profit came from:

- $16.3 million of unrealized gains on its tokens
- $3.18 million of unrealized staking income, up 41%
- a $106,228 realized loss on converting TRX

"Unrealized" means paper gains that rise or fall with the TRX price.

How the staking works: the company deposits TRX with JustLend, a lending app on the Tron network, and gets sTRX back. Each sTRX becomes worth more TRX over time as voting rewards and fees from renting out network "energy" build up. That rising exchange rate is what the company books as staking income.

**Who owns it**

The tokens were worth $257.8 million on Sept. 30, out of $275.2 million in total assets. Bravemorning Ltd., owned by director Weike Sun, held about 88.5% of the voting power, the filing says. The filing names Sun as the father of Tron founder Justin Sun and flags possible conflicts of interest, including with JustLend and the firm that set up the company's wallet.

The company also signed an at-the-market deal on Oct. 14 to sell up to $200 million of new stock. It had sold none by the filing date. On Oct. 18 it was elected one of the Tron network's 27 "Super Representatives," the validators that produce blocks, which pays rewards in TRX.

*In our opinion: this is a token treasury that happens to sell souvenirs, and the 10-Q says so in plain numbers. The figure to follow is the share count, because that $200 million stock program, if used, would split future profits further. The next filing will show whether any of it was tapped.*

articles.title: Goldman, Citi Among Banks Backing $270 Million Stablecoin, Report Says
articles.excerpt: The money covers five years of running costs for a planned U.S. issuer codenamed Project Faro. It has no chief executive yet and aims to launch in early 2027.
articles.body_md:
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank are among the banks that have committed about $270 million to a joint stablecoin company, [Bloomberg](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/goldman-citi-among-banks-in-270-million-stablecoin-backing) reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The money is meant to pay for five years of operations at the planned issuer, codenamed Project Faro, which is expected to be incorporated in the U.S., according to the report. None of the banks or the venture has commented publicly on it, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/goldman-citi-and-other-banks-reportedly-fund-270-million-stablecoin-initiative/) reported.

**Two issuers hold most of the market**

The bank group is going after a market that two companies dominate. Stablecoins in circulation totaled about $292.8 billion on Tuesday evening, with Tether's USDT at about $175.8 billion and Circle's USDC at about $70.0 billion, per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

**How a stablecoin issuer makes money**

A stablecoin is a token meant to stay worth $1. Buyers hand over dollars, and the issuer holds those dollars in reserve, mostly as cash and short-term government debt, so it can pay anyone back on request. The issuer keeps the interest the reserves earn. Project Faro's $270 million is a different pot: it pays for running the company, while the reserves would come from the people who buy the token.

**Twenty-one firms, no CEO yet**

The 21 firms said on Sept. 1 that they would form the company in the second half of 2026, subject to closing conditions. A dollar token comes first, with a euro version the next priority among other Group of Seven currencies, and the group is aiming for a commercial launch in the first half of 2027, [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/goldman-citi-join-global-banks-in-270-million-stablecoin-venture--bloomberg-5016335) reported. Members also include Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments and MUFG Bank.

The venture still has no name. It also has no chief executive; backers are still searching for one, per the report.

The reports don't say how much each bank is putting in, whether the money is equity, or which blockchain the token will use. The group has said it plans to follow the U.S. GENIUS Act and the EU's MiCA rules where they apply.

*In our opinion: the stake is the interest on reserves, which today goes mostly to Tether and Circle on about $246 billion of combined tokens. A bank-owned issuer would compete for that income with five years of running costs already paid for. The next checkable steps are a company name, a CEO hire and a chosen blockchain, and none of them exists yet.*

articles.title: SEC Filed 348 Enforcement Cases in Fiscal 2026, Down From 456
articles.excerpt: Money orders totaled $1.095 billion, the lowest since 2008 by a Reuters count. The SEC also set up a data office whose work includes tracing blockchain flows.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission brought 348 enforcement actions in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, the agency [said Tuesday](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-113-sec-announces-enforcement-annual-results-fiscal-year-2026), down from 456 the year before.

Money orders totaled $1.095 billion. That is the lowest level since 2008, according to a [Reuters review](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-10/us-sec-enforcement-activity-plummets-in-2026-with-fewer-fines-and-cases) of agency figures, which also put the median at 715 cases a year from 2005 to 2025.

**Where the $1.095 billion came from**

- Disgorgement and interest: $752 million
- Civil penalties: $343 million
- Returned to investors: about $731 million, to more than 250,000 people

A court in a separate, non-SEC case deemed $235 million of that disgorgement already satisfied, the release says.

How the categories work: disgorgement makes a defendant give back profits from the violation, while a civil penalty is a fine on top. Of the 348 actions, 235 were standalone cases. The other 113 were "follow-on" proceedings that bar people from parts of the industry after a criminal conviction or court order.

Two-thirds of standalone cases charged at least one individual. The agency also suspended trading 13 times over suspected manipulation of Asia-based companies' shares.

**A new office that reads blockchains**

The enforcement division launched an Office of Super Intelligence and Analytics, whose work includes "improved blockchain and financial-flow analysis," the release says. The SEC also signed an agreement with the CFTC on joint enforcement over products that span securities and derivatives. The release doesn't say how many fiscal 2026 cases involved crypto.

Chairman Paul Atkins said case counts and dollar totals "are not the only or most telling measures" of the program. Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the division had reviewed its docket and focused on "consequential misconduct."

*In our opinion: the case count fell about 24% in a year, and the agency's leaders say counts and dollar totals aren't the best yardstick. For crypto, the item to follow is the new analytics office and its blockchain tracing. Fiscal 2027's first filings will show what that work turns up.*
