articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $1.28 Billion in Worst Week Since June
articles.excerpt: Four of five sessions were red. BlackRock's IBIT alone lost about $1.21 billion; Fidelity's FBTC finished the week about $93 million ahead.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.28 billion from Nov. 2 through Nov. 6, their heaviest week of outflows since the week ended June 26, according to Farside Investors and SoSoValue data reported Saturday.

That is more than six times the $202.4 million that left the prior week. Ether ETFs lost another $365.3 million, extending a six-week outflow streak, SoSoValue shows.

A spot bitcoin ETF holds bitcoin and issues shares that trade on a stock exchange. When more shares are redeemed than created, the fund sells bitcoin and the day prints as a net outflow. Those daily prints are a public read on whether U.S. fund buyers are adding or cutting exposure.

**IBIT led the exits; FBTC finished green**

Farside's daily totals add to about $1.28 billion for the week: $398.6 million out Monday, $115.6 million Tuesday, $74.6 million in Wednesday, then $430.2 million and $411.9 million out Thursday and Friday. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for roughly $1.21 billion of the week's bitcoin-fund losses, including $403 million on Friday alone. Fidelity's FBTC took in about $93.1 million for the week, including a $236.7 million Wednesday inflow that partly offset later redemptions. Same product class, opposite week: IBIT bled, FBTC finished ahead.

SoSoValue puts Solana ETF outflows near $26.3 million and Hyperliquid products near $15.6 million for the same five sessions. Bitcoin traded near $75,690 at about noon ET Saturday, down 0.3% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

The prior worse week ended June 26, when the bitcoin funds shed about $1.79 billion. This week's total ranks among the largest weekly draws since the products launched in January 2024.

*In our opinion: the number worth chasing next is Monday's print after the U.S. close. A second straight heavy week would deepen the November hole; a quieter day would show whether Thursday and Friday were the bulk of the exit. Inside the $1.28 billion, Fidelity finished about $93 million ahead while IBIT alone accounted for roughly $1.21 billion of the loss.*

articles.title: Bitquery Traces $4.06M USDT Drains Across 365 TRON Wallets
articles.excerpt: Forty-three collector wallets shared one fee payer from Oct. 5 to Nov. 4. CertiK separately warned unpatched iPhones face DarkSword kit risk.
articles.body_md:
Blockchain data firm [Bitquery](https://bitquery.io/investigations/iphone-wallet-drain-tron-usdt) says at least $4.06 million in USDT left 365 TRON wallets between Oct. 5 and Nov. 4, routed to 43 short-lived collector addresses that all drew network fees from one common fee wallet.

The firm verified the on-chain figures on Nov. 5. It also counted 137,688 TRX taken from those addresses and at least $103,000 more emptied from 65 wallets on eight other chains, including Ethereum and BNB Chain.

**How the drains worked**

On TRON, moving USDT costs a fee paid in TRX. Bitquery says the fee wallet first sent a few TRX to a target address, then the whole USDT balance left for a collector within seconds, and leftover TRX followed. That pattern is how investigators linked the collectors. A shared fee wallet ties the money trail together; Bitquery says it does not by itself prove one operator controlled every theft.

Bitquery matched one Oct. 15 case, 16,428 USDT plus TRX 12 seconds later, to a published account from an iPhone owner who said they opened a video in Safari and tapped an ad. For the other addresses, the firm says the chain does not show which phone or wallet app held the seed phrase. It found no evidence of a flaw inside Trust Wallet or other apps; the risk it describes sits in device malware that searches phones for recovery phrases.

**Separate DarkSword warning**

Separately on Friday, auditor [CertiK](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/06/certik-warns-darksword-ios-exploit-can-target-crypto-wallets/) warned that a newer DarkSword iOS exploit kit is being used against unpatched iPhones, and that opening a malicious site in Safari can be enough. CertiK said the kit can pull Keychain data and search Photos and the Notes app for seed phrases, and listed MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Phantom, Exodus and Coinbase among apps whose on-device data can be targeted. It advised installing the latest iOS update, keeping seed phrases offline, and enabling Lockdown Mode for higher-risk users.

Bitquery's totals are a floor: only full-balance USDT empties tied to the fee wallet are counted. Most devices behind Bitquery's count remain unidentified. Bitquery has not attributed the full $4.06 million total to DarkSword alone.

*In our opinion: the next check for holders is the phone OS version and where the seed phrase lives. An updated iOS build and an offline phrase close the door these reports describe.*
